title: Giving up
hints: time.After(d) returns a channel that receives a value after d. Use it as one case of a select, with the result channel as the other.
Run fetch in a goroutine that sends its result on a channel. Give that channel a buffer of 1, so the goroutine can still finish and exit when you've stopped waiting for it.
ch := make(chan string, 1); go func() { ch <- fetch() }(); select { case v := <-ch: return v, nil; case <-time.After(d): return "", ErrTimeout }
